851:         >>> X, y = random_walk_blobs(n_ts_per_blob=100, sz=256, d=1, n_blobs=3)
852:         >>> clf = LearningShapelets(n_shapelets_per_size={10: 5}, max_iter=1,
853:         ...                     verbose=0)
854:         >>> clf.fit(X, y).get_weights("classification")[0].shape
855:         (5, 3)
856:         >>> clf.get_weights("shapelets_0")[0].shape
857:         (5, 10, 1)
858:         >>> len(clf.get_weights("shapelets_0"))
859:         1
860:         """
861:         if layer_name is None:
862:             return self.model_.get_weights()
863:         else:
864:             return self.model_.get_layer(layer_name).get_weights()
865: 
866:     def set_weights(self, weights, layer_name=None):
867:         """Set model weights (or weights for a given layer if `layer_name`
868:         is provided).
869: 
870:         Parameters
871:         ----------
872:         weights: list of ndarrays
873:             Weights to set for the model / target layer
874: 
875:         layer_name: str or None (default: None)
876:             Name of the layer for which  weights should be set.
877:             If None, all model weights are set.
878:             Available layer names with weights are:
879: 
880:             - "shapelets_i_j" with i an integer for the shapelet id and j an
881:               integer for the dimension
882:             - "classification" for the final classification layer
883: 
884:         Examples
885:         --------
886:         >>> from tslearn.generators import random_walk_blobs
887:         >>> X, y = random_walk_blobs(n_ts_per_blob=10, sz=16, d=1, n_blobs=3)
888:         >>> clf = LearningShapelets(n_shapelets_per_size={3: 1}, max_iter=1,
889:         ...                     verbose=0)
890:         >>> _ = clf.fit(X, y)
891:         >>> weights_shapelet = [
892:         ...     numpy.array([[[1], [2], [3]]])
893:         ... ]
894:         >>> clf.set_weights(weights_shapelet, layer_name="shapelets_0")
895:         >>> clf.shapelets_as_time_series_
896:         array([[[1.],
897:                 [2.],
898:                 [3.]]])
899:         """
900:         if layer_name is None:
901:             return self.model_.set_weights(weights)
902:         else:
903:             return self.model_.get_layer(layer_name).set_weights(weights)
904: 
905:     def _is_fitted(self):
906:         check_is_fitted(self, 'model_')
907:         return True
908: 
909:     def _to_dict(self, output=None, hyper_parameters_only=False):
910:         result = super()._to_dict(output, hyper_parameters_only)
911: 
912:         # In case optimizer is a keras optimizer, leaves string unchanged
913:         result["hyper_params"]["optimizer"] = serialize_keras_object(
914:             result["hyper_params"]["optimizer"]
915:         )
916:         return result
917: 
918:     def _get_model_params(self):
919:         """Get model parameters that are sufficient to recapitulate it."""
920:         params = super()._get_model_params()
921:         params.update({"_X_fit_dims": self._X_fit_dims,
922:                        "model_": self.model_.to_json(),
923:                        "model_weights_": self.get_weights()})
924:         return params
925: 
926:     @staticmethod
927:     def _organize_model(cls, model):
928:         """
929:         Instantiate the model with all hyper-parameters,
930:         set all model parameters and then return the model.
931:         Do not use directly. Use the designated classmethod to load a model.
932:         Parameters
933:         ----------
934:         cls : instance of model that inherits from `BaseModelPackage`
935:             a model instance
936:         model : dict
937:             Model dict containing hyper-parameters and model-parameters
938:         Returns
939:         -------
940:         model: instance of model that inherits from `BaseModelPackage`
941:             instance of the model class with hyper-parameters and
942:             model parameters set from the passed model dict
943:         """
944: 
945:         model_params = model.pop('model_params')
946:         hyper_params = model.pop('hyper_params')  # hyper-params
947: 
948:         # In case optimizer is a keras optimizer, leaves string unchanged
949:         hyper_params["optimizer"] = deserialize_keras_object(
950:             hyper_params["optimizer"]
951:         )
952: 
953:         if hyper_params["n_shapelets_per_size"]:
954:             # Keys are encoded with strings in json
955:             hyper_params["n_shapelets_per_size"] = {
956:                 int(sz): nb for sz, nb in
957:                 hyper_params["n_shapelets_per_size"].items()
958:             }
959: 
960:         # instantiate with hyperparameters
961:         inst = cls(**hyper_params)
962: 
963:         if "model_" in model_params.keys():
964:             # set all model params
965:             inst.model_ = model_from_json(
966:                 model_params.pop("model_"),
967:                 custom_objects={
968:                     "LocalSquaredDistanceLayer": LocalSquaredDistanceLayer,
969:                     "GlobalMinPooling1D": GlobalMinPooling1D,
970:                     "PatchingLayer": PatchingLayer,
971:                 }
972:             )
973:             inst.set_weights(model_params.pop("model_weights_"))
974:         for p in model_params.keys():
975:             if p == "n_shapelets_per_size_":
976:                 # Keys are encoded with strings in json
977:                 model_params[p] = {
978:                     int(sz): nb for sz, nb in model_params[p].items()
979:                 }
980:             setattr(inst, p, model_params[p])
981:         inst._X_fit_dims = tuple(inst._X_fit_dims)
982:         inst._build_auxiliary_models()
983: 
984:         return inst
985: 
986:     def to_hdf5(self, path):
987:         """LearningShapelet is not HDF5 serializable"""
988:         check_is_fitted(self, 'model_')
989:         raise NotImplementedError("LearningShapelet is not HDF5 serializable")
990: 
991:     def _more_tags(self):
992:         tags = super()._more_tags()
993:         tags.update({'allow_nan': True, 'allow_variable_length': True})
994:         return tags
995: 
996:     def __sklearn_tags__(self):
997:         tags = super().__sklearn_tags__()
998:         tags.input_tags.allow_nan = True
999:         tags.allow_variable_length = True
1000:         return tags
